problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-1,-1),(0,-1),$ and $(0,0).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(4,-1)$
- $(0,0)$
- $(-4,-8)$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(1,3)$, $(-2,0)$ and $(2,-1).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(8,-16)$
- $(-6,12)$
- $(8,16)$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -6 & 8 \\ 6 & 12 & -16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are $(-3,6)$, $(-6,12)$ and $(8,-16).$ 

So, the correct answer is "I and II only."
